clue.text: Get one's own back

parts.note: reads like taking revenge, but literally means recovering property that belongs to you, as a lender does with goods unpaid for

explanation.surface: Someone vows revenge on a person who wronged them.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back goods whose payments have lapsed is literally to recover your own property again.

clue.text: Respond to plea to return to the stage

definitions.meaning: to answer or reply to an appeal
split as ..., to act once more in the theatre

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as RE- (again) plus ACT, performing on stage a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Responding to something is reacting; acting again on stage is re-acting, the same letters split.

clue.text: Publicist covers new lines in lager

indicators.note: the outer piece wraps around the rearranged letters, covering them

parts.note: PR, public relations, stands for a publicist

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of the word lines are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A press agent writes fresh copy for a beer advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: PR, short for public relations, stands in for a publicist here, a slight stretch the solver must accept.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilsner is a pale Czech style of lager beer named after the city of Pilsen.

clue.text: Reacted like a startled horse and threw

definitions.meaning: a frightened horse jumps sideways or rears away
past tense of shy, meaning to fling or toss, as at a coconut shy

explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts, which explains the throwing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the past tense of the verb shy: to start away in fright, and to fling.

clue.text: Defile and glen in the country

indicators.note: to defile is to corrupt or spoil, so the letters that follow are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A narrow pass and a valley set in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defile' looks like a noun for a narrow mountain pass, fitting glen, but it is the verb, signalling the letters of AND GLEN are mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: England is the country, one of the nations of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Mock the northern city's affectation

indicators.note: an affectation is something put on or altered from the natural, so the letters are altered

parts.note: taken as written
the word city with its possessive s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at the pretensions of a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affectation' rearranges THE plus N plus CITYS. 'Mock' looks like a verb meaning ridicule but is the adjective meaning imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mock is fake or imitation, as synthetic materials are man-made copies of natural ones.

clue.text: Attempt to form a party

definitions.meaning: to have a ... at something is to have a try
an informal word for a lively celebration

explanation.surface: Trying to throw a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is both an informal go at something and a slang word for a festive gathering.

clue.text: Bird of the frozen North

parts.note: bitter describes intensely cold weather, as in a bitter wind

explanation.surface: A bird that lives in the icy Arctic regions.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER for frozen relies on the sense of piercing cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading bird of the heron family, known for its booming call.

clue.text: Refused it anyway, having had more than enough

indicators.note: anyway suggests the letters can be arranged in any way at all

explanation.surface: Someone declined the dish since they had already eaten plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' rearranges REFUSEDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be surfeited is to have been supplied to excess, overfull with food or anything else.

clue.text: Encircled friend making a comeback

annotationWithheld.why: Encircled friend making a comeback (8): ALLY inside RING gives the answer, but no clue word supplies RING apart from Encircled, which would then be both the container's letters and its indicator

clue.text: Kind disposition

definitions.meaning: kind as a noun, meaning sort or type
a person's innate character or temperament

explanation.definitionFit: Nature means both the type of a thing and the inborn character of a person.

clue.text: Severely punished for being drunk

definitions.meaning: executed by having rocks thrown, an ancient penalty
slang for heavily intoxicated by alcohol or drugs

explanation.surface: A person was punished harshly for intoxication.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned means both pelted with rocks as a punishment and, in slang, very intoxicated.

clue.text: Runners allowed to enter various heats

indicators.note: the piece for allowed goes inside the rearranged letters, entering them
various suggests different arrangements of the letters of heats

parts.note: let means allowed, as in let go

explanation.surface: Competitors are admitted to the different qualifying races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heats' looks like part of the race picture, but it is only the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes are sportspeople, and runners are a prime example of track athletes.

clue.text: Wit of an animated priest

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: The humour of a lively clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' rearranges PRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is a French borrowing meaning liveliness of mind, sparkling wit.

clue.text: Stay to eat and drink

parts.note: to sup is to take supper, to eat
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Remain for dinner and drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like an instruction to remain but is the noun: a stay is a prop or support.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a brace or prop, something that holds a thing up, as a supporter does.

clue.text: Sheridan's competitors?

parts.note: seems to ask who opposed Sheridan, but refers to the title of the 18th-century comedy by playwright Richard Brinsley Sheridan

explanation.surface: Who were Sheridan's opponents?
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was an Irish playwright whose best-known comedies include a 1775 play about suitors in Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Sheridan's play literally names people who compete, so it is his competitors.

clue.text: Set off for school in time

indicators.note: the school's name sits inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Leave for school on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as leaving for school but means to cause to explode. Eton College is a famous private boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to detonate it, causing it to explode.

clue.text: Notice fewer without blemish

parts.note: to spot is to notice or catch sight of
less is a looser word for fewer

explanation.surface: Seeing fewer flaws until there are none.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means perfectly clean, having no marks or stains at all.

clue.text: They take the strain out of brewing

definitions.text: They take the strain out of brewing

parts.words: They take the strain out of brewing
parts.note: sounds like relieving stress, but means they strain leaves when you make a cuppa, so no strainer is needed

explanation.surface: Something that makes brewing less stressful.
explanation.definitionFit: Small porous sachets hold leaves so the brewed drink needs no straining afterwards.

clue.text: Meeting that has no standing?

parts.note: suggests an unofficial gathering, but means a meeting at which everyone is seated

explanation.surface: A gathering with no official status.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a meeting comes from Latin for sitting, so its members do no standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal sitting of a court or council is a meeting held seated.

clue.text: They make us cold and wet

definitions.text: They make us cold and wet

indicators.note: make here means form or produce, so the following letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A grumble about those who leave us chilly and soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges US COLD, and the whole clue doubles as the definition: grey skies leave us chilly and soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain falls from these masses of vapour overhead, which also block the warming sunshine.

clue.text: In this world, or possibly another

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: In this life or perhaps a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ANOTHER; the surface plays on this world versus another world.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means here among the living, in this world, as in heaven on earth.

clue.text: He lacked a fourth at bridge

definitions.text: He lacked a fourth at bridge

parts.words: He lacked a fourth at bridge
parts.note: sounds like a card player short of a partner, but refers to the Roman hero who held a bridge over the Tiber with only two companions

explanation.surface: A card player could not find a fourth for his game.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge game needs four players; the Roman legend, told in Macaulay's poem, had three men defending the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend this Roman soldier defended the Sublician bridge with just two others, three in all.

clue.text: Oil found somewhere in southeast Europe, say

indicators.note: say tells us the country's name is spoken aloud to give a word with the same sound

parts.note: a country in southeast Europe, the Hellenic Republic

explanation.surface: Oil discovered in a Balkan land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that the country of Greece is heard as a word for oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is a thick oily lubricant, and to grease is to oil.

clue.text: Sail out of port

definitions.meaning: a large triangular jib sail used on yachts
an Italian seaport on the Ligurian coast

explanation.surface: A ship sails out of harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is a major Italian port, and the large foresail used on racing yachts carries its name.

clue.text: A Spaniard of Norse extraction

indicators.note: extraction suggests the letters are pulled out and reworked, while the surface reads it as ancestry

explanation.surface: A Spanish man with Scandinavian ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraction' rearranges NORSE; in the surface it means descent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish title for a gentleman, equivalent to Mr, stands for a Spanish man.

clue.text: A sweet's round and in layers

indicators.note: round means turned around, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a tart is a sweet pastry, and the possessive gives its s

explanation.surface: A dessert that is circular and built up in tiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns ATARTS backwards. 'A sweet's' is A TART'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, such as the bands of rock laid down over time.

clue.text: At sea no rating is lacking in knowledge

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor of no rank is uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges NORATING. A rating is a naval sailor below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means uninformed, lacking knowledge or awareness.

clue.text: Build-up of runs — they may retain the Ashes

indicators.note: building up the letters from scratch means putting them together in a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket side scores heavily in the hope of keeping the Ashes trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Build-up of' rearranges RUNS. The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket series, its trophy a tiny urn; runs are cricket's points.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vessels used to hold the cremated remains of the dead.

clue.text: One suffering heat burns

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are distressed into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone enduring the heat gets sunburnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges HEATBURNS, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying in the sun who overdoes it ends up burnt by its heat.
